sanskrit: giriprasthe tu sā yasmin sthitā svasitalocanā sa savṛkṣakṣupalato hiraṇmaya ivābhavat
english: The mountain slope on which she stood, her eyes bright as a white blossom, glowed as though fashioned of gold — trees, shrubs, and all.

sanskrit: avamene ca tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ vapuḥ avāptaṃ cātmano mene sa rājā cakṣuṣaḥ phalam
english: Beholding her, the king deemed her form surpassing that of every living creature; and he felt that his eyes had at last gained their true reward.

sanskrit: janmaprabhṛti yat kiṃ cid dṛṣṭavān sa mahīpatiḥ rūpaṃ na sadṛśaṃ tasyās tarkayām āsa kiṃ cana
english: From the day of his birth the great king had seen many things, yet he reflected that he had never beheld any beauty comparable to hers.

sanskrit: tayā baddhamanaścakṣuḥ pāśair guṇamayais tadā na cacāla tato deśād bubudhe na ca kiṃ cana
english: His mind and eyes were bound by the cords woven from her virtues; he stirred not from that spot, and knew nothing of what passed around him.

sanskrit: asyā nūnaṃ viśālākṣyāḥ sadevāsuramānuṣam lokaṃ nirmathya dhātredaṃ rūpam āviṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam
english: "Surely," he thought, "the Creator churned the whole world — gods, asuras, and men alike — and brought forth this form of the wide-eyed one."

sanskrit: evaṃ sa tarkayām āsa rūpadraviṇasaṃpadā kanyām asadṛśīṃ loke nṛpaḥ saṃvaraṇas tadā
english: Thus did King Saṃvaraṇa reason to himself, marvelling at the treasure of her beauty, a maiden unequalled anywhere in the world.

sanskrit: tāṃ ca dṛṣṭvaiva kalyāṇīṃ kalyāṇābhijano nṛpaḥ jagāma manasā cintāṃ kāmamārgaṇapīḍitaḥ
english: That king of noble lineage, having gazed upon the auspicious maiden, fell into deep anxious thought, tormented by the arrows of desire.

sanskrit: dahyamānaḥ sa tīvreṇa nṛpatir manmathāgninā apragalbhāṃ pragalbhaḥ sa tām uvāca yaśasvinīm
english: Burning fiercely in the fire of Kāma, the bold king, though she was reticent, spoke to that renowned maiden.

sanskrit: kāsi kasyāsi rambhoru kimarthaṃ ceha tiṣṭhasi kathaṃ ca nirjane 'raṇye carasy ekā śucismite
english: "Who are you, O round-thighed one? Whose are you? For what purpose do you stand here? And how, O pure-smiling one, do you roam alone in this deserted forest?"

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi sarvānavadyāṅgī sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā vibhūṣaṇam ivaiteṣāṃ bhūṣaṇānām abhīpsitam
english: "You are blameless in every limb, adorned with every ornament; and yet you seem yourself to be the desired ornament of all these ornaments."

sanskrit: na devīṃ nāsurīṃ caiva na yakṣīṃ na ca rākṣasīm na ca bhogavatīṃ manye na gandharvīṃ na mānuṣīm
english: "I take you for neither a goddess nor an asura-woman, neither a yakṣī nor a rākṣasī, neither a serpent-princess of Bhogavatī, nor a gandharva-maiden, nor a mortal."

sanskrit: yā hi dṛṣṭā mayā kāś cic chrutā vāpi varāṅganāḥ na tāsāṃ sadṛśīṃ manye tvām ahaṃ mattakāśini
english: "Of all the beautiful women I have ever seen or heard of, I do not consider you the equal of any of them, O woman whose eyes are full and intoxicating."

sanskrit: evaṃ tāṃ sa mahīpālo babhāṣe na tu sā tadā kāmārtaṃ nirjane 'raṇye pratyabhāṣata kiṃ cana
english: Thus did the king address her; but she, in that solitary forest, did not reply a single word to the love-stricken man.

sanskrit: tato lālapyamānasya pārthivasyāyatekṣaṇā saudāminīva sābhreṣu tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Then, as the king entreated her further, the large-eyed one vanished on that very spot, like a flash of lightning amid clouds.

sanskrit: tām anvicchan sa nṛpatiḥ paricakrāma tat tadā vanaṃ vanajapatrākṣīṃ bhramann unmattavat tadā
english: Seeking her, the king wandered through that forest, eyes like lotus petals, roaming about like one who had lost his wits.

sanskrit: apaśyamānaḥ sa tu tāṃ bahu tatra vilapya ca niśceṣṭaḥ kauravaśreṣṭho muhūrtaṃ sa vyatiṣṭhata
english: Not finding her, and having lamented greatly in that place, the foremost of the Kauravas stood motionless for a while, all movement ceased in him.

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca atha tasyām adṛśyāyāṃ nṛpatiḥ kāmamohitaḥ pātanaḥ śatrusaṃghānāṃ papāta dharaṇītale
english: The Gandharva said: When she vanished from sight, the king, deluded by desire — he who was the feller of enemy hosts — fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite bhūmāv atha sā cāruhāsinī punaḥ pīnāyataśroṇī darśayām āsa taṃ nṛpam
english: When he had fallen upon the earth, that lovely-smiling, full and shapely-hipped woman revealed herself to the king once more.

sanskrit: athābabhāṣe kalyāṇī vācā madhurayā nṛpam taṃ kurūṇāṃ kulakaraṃ kāmābhihatacetasam
english: Then the auspicious one spoke in a sweet voice to that king, founder of the Kuru line, whose mind was struck down by desire.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhadraṃ te na tvam arhasy ariṃdama mohaṃ nṛpatiśārdūla gantum āviṣkṛtaḥ kṣitau
english: "Arise, arise! May fortune be yours! O subduer of foes, O tiger among kings, you ought not to yield to such delusion, lying exposed upon the earth."

sanskrit: evam ukto 'tha nṛpatir vācā madhurayā tadā dadarśa vipulaśroṇīṃ tām evābhimukhe sthitām
english: Thus addressed by her sweet voice, the king looked up and saw her — broad-hipped and fair — standing directly before him.

sanskrit: atha tām asitāpāṅgīm ābabhāṣe narādhipaḥ manmathāgniparītātmā saṃdigdhākṣarayā girā
english: Then the lord of men, his soul consumed by the fire of Kāma, spoke to her of dark-tinged eyes in a voice uncertain and faltering.

sanskrit: sādhu mām asitāpāṅge kāmārtaṃ mattakāśini bhajasva bhajamānaṃ māṃ prāṇā hi prajahanti mām
english: "O dark-eyed one, O woman with full and bright eyes, favour me who am tormented by desire and who devotedly seeks you — for life is departing from me."

sanskrit: tvadarthaṃ hi viśālākṣi mām ayaṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ kāmaḥ kamalagarbhābhe pratividhyan na śāmyati
english: "For your sake, O wide-eyed one, O woman bright as the interior of a lotus, Kāma pierces me with his sharp arrows and does not abate."

sanskrit: grastam evam anākrande bhadre kāmamahāhinā sā tvaṃ pīnāyataśroṇi paryāpnuhi śubhānane
english: "I am seized by the great serpent of desire and there is none to hear my cry, O fortunate one — O full-hipped, auspicious-faced woman, rescue me."

sanskrit: tvayy adhīnā hi me prāṇāḥ kiṃnarodgītabhāṣiṇi cārusarvānavadyāṅgi padmendusadṛśānane
english: "My life depends entirely on you, O woman whose voice is like the song of a kiṃnara, whose every limb is beautiful and blameless, whose face resembles both the lotus and the moon."

sanskrit: na hy ahaṃ tvad ṛte bhīru śakṣye jīvitum ātmanā tasmāt kuru viśālākṣi mayy anukrośam aṅgane
english: "Without you, O timid one, I cannot sustain my life. Therefore, O wide-eyed woman, O graceful one, show compassion toward me."

sanskrit: bhaktaṃ mām asitāpāṅge na parityaktum arhasi tvaṃ hi māṃ prītiyogena trātum arhasi bhāmini
english: "O dark-eyed one, you must not abandon me who am devoted to you. You have the power to save me with the bond of love, O passionate woman."

sanskrit: gāndharveṇa ca māṃ bhīru vivāhenaihi sundari vivāhānāṃ hi rambhoru gāndharvaḥ śreṣṭha ucyate
english: "Come, O timid one, beautiful woman, take me in the Gāndharva form of marriage — for of all marriage rites, O round-thighed one, the Gāndharva is said to be the highest."

sanskrit: tapaty uvāca nāham īśātmano rājan kanyā pitṛmatī hy aham mayi ced asti te prītir yācasva pitaraṃ mama
english: Tapatī said: I am not mistress of my own person, O king — I am a maiden who has a father. If you truly love me, then go and ask my father.

sanskrit: yathā hi te mayā prāṇāḥ saṃgṛhītā nareśvara darśanād eva bhūyas tvaṃ tathā prāṇān mamāharaḥ
english: "Just as you say your life has been seized by me, O lord of men, know too that at the very sight of you you have likewise taken away my life."

sanskrit: na cāham īśā dehasya tasmān nṛpatisattama samīpaṃ nopagacchāmi na svatantrā hi yoṣitaḥ
english: "Yet I am not free to dispose of my own body; therefore, O best of kings, I cannot draw near you — women are not independent."

sanskrit: kā hi sarveṣu lokeṣu viśrutābhijanaṃ nṛpam kanyā nābhilaṣen nāthaṃ bhartāraṃ bhaktavatsalam
english: "What maiden in all the worlds would not desire a king of celebrated lineage as her lord and husband, one who is kind and devoted to those who love him?"

sanskrit: tasmād evaṃgate kāle yācasva pitaraṃ mama ādityaṃ praṇipātena tapasā niyamena ca
english: "Therefore, in this situation, go and entreat my father, the sun-god Āditya, with prostrations, austerities, and observances."

sanskrit: sa cet kāmayate dātuṃ tava mām arimardana bhaviṣyāmy atha te rājan satataṃ vaśavartinī
english: "If he wishes to give me to you, O crusher of foes, then, O king, I shall forever be obedient to you."

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi tapatī nāma sāvitryavarajā sutā asya lokapradīpasya savituḥ kṣatriyarṣabha
english: "I am Tapatī by name, the younger sister of Sāvitrī, daughter of Savitṛ — of the sun who is the lamp of the world — O bull among kṣatriyas."

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca evam uktvā tatas tūrṇaṃ jagāmordhvam aninditā sa tu rājā punar bhūmau tatraiva nipapāta ha
english: The Gandharva said: Having spoken thus, the blameless one swiftly rose upward; and the king fell once more upon the ground on that very spot.

sanskrit: amātyaḥ sānuyātras tu taṃ dadarśa mahāvane kṣitau nipatitaṃ kāle śakradhvajam ivocchritam
english: The minister who had accompanied him found him in the great forest, fallen to the ground like the banner of Indra that has been cast down.

sanskrit: taṃ hi dṛṣṭvā maheṣvāsaṃ niraśvaṃ patitaṃ kṣitau babhūva so 'sya sacivaḥ saṃpradīpta ivāgninā
english: Seeing that great archer horseless and fallen to earth, the minister was as though set ablaze by fire.

sanskrit: tvarayā copasaṃgamya snehād āgatasaṃbhramaḥ taṃ samutthāpayām āsa nṛpatiṃ kāmamohitam
english: He hastened to him with the agitation that love brings, and raised up the king who was dazed by desire.

sanskrit: bhūtalād bhūmipāleśaṃ piteva patitaṃ sutam prajñayā vayasā caiva vṛddhaḥ kīrtyā damena ca
english: Like a father lifting a fallen son from the ground, that minister — aged in wisdom, years, fame, and self-restraint — raised up the lord of earth.

sanskrit: amātyas taṃ samutthāpya babhūva vigatajvaraḥ uvāca cainaṃ kalyāṇyā vācā madhurayotthitam mā bhair manujaśārdūla bhadraṃ cāstu tavānagha
english: Having raised the king, the minister's own anguish faded; and he spoke to him who had just risen, with auspicious, sweet words: "Fear not, O tiger among men; may good fortune be yours, O sinless one."

sanskrit: kṣutpipāsāpariśrāntaṃ tarkayām āsa taṃ nṛpam patitaṃ pātanaṃ saṃkhye śātravāṇāṃ mahītale
english: He surmised that the king — he who fells enemies in battle — had fallen to the ground overcome by hunger, thirst, and exhaustion.

sanskrit: vāriṇātha suśītena śiras tasyābhyaṣecayat aspṛśan mukuṭaṃ rājñaḥ puṇḍarīkasugandhinā
english: He then sprinkled the king's head with very cool water fragrant as the white lotus, taking care not to disturb the royal crown.

sanskrit: tataḥ pratyāgataprāṇas tad balaṃ balavān nṛpaḥ sarvaṃ visarjayām āsa tam ekaṃ sacivaṃ vinā
english: When the powerful king had recovered his life-breath, he dismissed the entire army, retaining only that one minister.

sanskrit: tatas tasyājñayā rājño vipratasthe mahad balam sa tu rājā giriprasthe tasmin punar upāviśat
english: By the king's command, the great army marched away; and the king sat down once more upon that mountain slope.

sanskrit: tatas tasmin girivare śucir bhūtvā kṛtāñjaliḥ ārirādhayiṣuḥ sūryaṃ tasthāv ūrdhvabhujaḥ kṣitau
english: Then, on that excellent mountain, he became ritually pure, joined his palms in supplication, and stood upon the ground with arms raised, desiring to propitiate the sun.

sanskrit: jagāma manasā caiva vasiṣṭham ṛṣisattamam purohitam amitraghnas tadā saṃvaraṇo nṛpaḥ
english: And in his mind, King Saṃvaraṇa — the slayer of foes — turned also to Vasiṣṭha, the best of seers, his own household priest.

sanskrit: naktaṃdinam athaikasthe sthite tasmiñ janādhipe athājagāma viprarṣis tadā dvādaśame 'hani
english: As the lord of the people remained thus in that solitary place through nights and days alike, the seer among brāhmaṇas came to him on the twelfth day.

sanskrit: sa viditvaiva nṛpatiṃ tapatyā hṛtamānasam divyena vidhinā jñātvā bhāvitātmā mahān ṛṣiḥ
english: That great and cultivated-souled seer, knowing by divine means that the king's heart had been taken by Tapatī, understood all.

sanskrit: tathā tu niyatātmānaṃ sa taṃ nṛpatisattamam ābabhāṣe sa dharmātmā tasyaivārthacikīrṣayā
english: That righteous-souled one then addressed the best of kings, who had been disciplining his self thus, desiring to accomplish his purpose.

sanskrit: sa tasya manujendrasya paśyato bhagavān ṛṣiḥ ūrdhvam ācakrame draṣṭuṃ bhāskaraṃ bhāskaradyutiḥ
english: While the lord of men watched, the blessed seer, radiant as the sun himself, ascended upward to behold the sun.

sanskrit: sahasrāṃśuṃ tato vipraḥ kṛtāñjalir upasthitaḥ vasiṣṭho 'ham iti prītyā sa cātmānaṃ nyavedayat
english: Standing before the thousand-rayed one with joined palms, Vasiṣṭha gladly made himself known, saying: "I am Vasiṣṭha."

sanskrit: tam uvāca mahātejā vivasvān munisattamam maharṣe svāgataṃ te 'stu kathayasva yathecchasi
english: Vivasvān, of great splendour, then said to the best of sages: "Welcome to you, O great seer — speak freely of whatever you wish."

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca yaiṣā te tapatī nāma sāvitryavarajā sutā tāṃ tvāṃ saṃvaraṇasyārthe varayāmi vibhāvaso
english: Vasiṣṭha said: This daughter of yours named Tapatī, the younger sister of Sāvitrī — I ask you for her hand on behalf of Saṃvaraṇa, O Vibhāvasu.

sanskrit: sa hi rājā bṛhatkīrtir dharmārthavid udāradhīḥ yuktaḥ saṃvaraṇo bhartā duhitus te vihaṃgama
english: "For that king Saṃvaraṇa is of great fame, learned in dharma and wealth, of noble mind — a fitting husband for your daughter, O one who roams the sky."

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca ity uktaḥ savitā tena dadānīty eva niścitaḥ pratyabhāṣata taṃ vipraṃ pratinandya divākaraḥ
english: The Gandharva said: Thus addressed by Vasiṣṭha, Savitā the day-maker, resolved to give her, welcomed the seer and replied.

sanskrit: varaḥ saṃvaraṇo rājñāṃ tvam ṛṣīṇāṃ varo mune tapatī yoṣitāṃ śreṣṭhā kim anyatrāpavarjanāt
english: "Saṃvaraṇa is the best among kings; you are the best among sages, O muni; Tapatī is the best among women — what reason could there be for refusal?"

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvānavadyāgnīṃ tapatīṃ tapanaḥ svayam dadau saṃvaraṇasyārthe vasiṣṭhāya mahātmane pratijagrāha tāṃ kanyāṃ maharṣis tapatīṃ tadā
english: Then Tapana himself gave the blameless Tapatī — resplendent as fire — for Saṃvaraṇa's sake to the great-souled Vasiṣṭha; and the great seer accepted that maiden Tapatī.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭho 'tha visṛṣṭaś ca punar evājagāma ha yatra vikhyatakīrtiḥ sa kurūṇām ṛṣabho 'bhavat
english: Vasiṣṭha, having been sent off, came back again to the place where that bull of the Kurus of celebrated fame was waiting.

sanskrit: sa rājā manmathāviṣṭas tadgatenāntarātmanā dṛṣṭvā ca devakanyāṃ tāṃ tapatīṃ cāruhāsinīm vasiṣṭhena sahāyāntīṃ saṃhṛṣṭo 'bhyadhikaṃ babhau
english: That king, who had been possessed by Kāma and whose inner self had dwelt entirely on her, seeing that goddess-daughter, the lovely-smiling Tapatī, coming with Vasiṣṭha, was filled with exceeding joy.

sanskrit: kṛcchre dvādaśarātre tu tasya rājñaḥ samāpite ājagāma viśuddhātmā vasiṣṭho bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
english: When the king's twelve nights of arduous vigil had been completed, the pure-souled, blessed seer Vasiṣṭha arrived.

sanskrit: tapasārādhya varadaṃ devaṃ gopatim īśvaram lebhe saṃvaraṇo bhāryāṃ vasiṣṭhasyaiva tejasā
english: Having propitiated through austerities the boon-granting god, the lord and master of the cattle of the sky, Saṃvaraṇa obtained his wife by the very power of Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: tatas tasmin giriśreṣṭhe devagandharvasevite jagrāha vidhivat pāṇiṃ tapatyāḥ sa nararṣabhaḥ
english: Then on that most excellent mountain, frequented by gods and gandharvas, that bull among men took Tapatī's hand according to the rites.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhenābhyanujñātas tasminn eva dharādhare so 'kāmayata rājarṣir vihartuṃ saha bhāryayā
english: Permitted by Vasiṣṭha, that royal seer desired to dwell on that same mountain range in the company of his wife.

sanskrit: tataḥ pure ca rāṣṭre ca vāhaneṣu baleṣu ca ādideśa mahīpālas tam eva sacivaṃ tadā
english: Thereupon the lord of earth gave command over the city, the realm, the transport, and the armies to that same minister.

sanskrit: nṛpatiṃ tv abhyanujñāya vasiṣṭho 'thāpacakrame so 'pi rājā girau tasmin vijahārāmaropamaḥ
english: Vasiṣṭha then took his leave of the king and departed; and the king too sported on that mountain, like one equal to an immortal.

sanskrit: tato dvādaśa varṣāṇi kānaneṣu jaleṣu ca reme tasmin girau rājā tayaiva saha bhāryayā
english: For twelve years the king took his pleasure on that mountain, in its forests and waters, together with his wife alone.

sanskrit: tasya rājñaḥ pure tasmin samā dvādaśa sarvaśaḥ na vavarṣa sahasrākṣo rāṣṭre caivāsya sarvaśaḥ
english: During those twelve years, throughout that king's city and throughout all his realm, the thousand-eyed Indra sent no rain whatsoever.

sanskrit: tat kṣudhārtair nirānandaiḥ śavabhūtais tadā naraiḥ abhavat pretarājasya puraṃ pretair ivāvṛtam
english: That city then, with its people tormented by hunger, joyless, and reduced to the state of corpses, looked like the city of the king of the dead, crowded with ghosts.

sanskrit: tatas tat tādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa eva bhagavān ṛṣiḥ abhyapadyata dharmātmā vasiṣṭho rājasattamam
english: Seeing the city in such a state, that same blessed seer — righteous-souled Vasiṣṭha — went to the best of kings.

sanskrit: taṃ ca pārthivaśārdūlam ānayām āsa tat puram tapatyā sahitaṃ rājann uṣitaṃ dvādaśīḥ samāḥ
english: He brought that tiger among kings back to his city — O king — together with Tapatī, after his having sojourned twelve years away.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravṛṣṭas tatrāsīd yathāpūrvaṃ surārihā tasmin nṛpatiśārdūle praviṣṭe nagaraṃ punaḥ
english: Then, as that tiger among kings re-entered his city, the slayer of the enemies of the gods — Indra — caused rain to fall there as in former times.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarāṣṭraṃ mumude tat puraṃ parayā mudā tena pārthivamukhyena bhāvitaṃ bhāvitātmanā
english: Then that city, together with the whole kingdom, rejoiced with the greatest joy, enlivened by that foremost of kings, himself of enlivened soul.

sanskrit: tato dvādaśa varṣāṇi punar īje narādhipaḥ patnyā tapatyā sahito yathā śakro marutpatiḥ
english: Thereafter the lord of men performed sacrifice for twelve more years together with his wife Tapatī, just as Śakra the lord of the Maruts does.

sanskrit: evam āsīn mahābhāgā tapatī nāma paurvikī tava vaivasvatī pārtha tāpatyas tvaṃ yayā mataḥ
english: Such was she — the greatly blessed Tapatī of ancient times, daughter of Vivasvat — O Pārtha; and it is from her that you are known as Tāpatya.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ saṃjanayām āsa kuruṃ saṃvaraṇo nṛpaḥ tapatyāṃ tapatāṃ śreṣṭha tāpatyas tvaṃ tato 'rjuna
english: King Saṃvaraṇa begot upon Tapatī the ancestor Kuru, O best of those who blaze with splendour; from her descent you are called Tāpatya, O Arjuna.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa gandharvavacaḥ śrutvā tat tadā bharatarṣabha arjunaḥ parayā prītyā pūrṇacandra ivābabhau
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard those words of the gandharva, Arjuna, O bull of the Bhārata line, shone with the greatest delight, like the full moon.

sanskrit: uvāca ca maheṣvāso gandharvaṃ kurusattamaḥ jātakautūhalo 'tīva vasiṣṭhasya tapobalāt
english: And that great archer, best of the Kurus, deeply curious about the power of Vasiṣṭha's austerity, spoke to the gandharva.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha iti yasyaitad ṛṣer nāma tvayeritam etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ yathāvat tad vadasva me
english: "This name of the seer 'Vasiṣṭha' that you have uttered — I wish to hear the full account of it. Tell me truly."
